task_context.problem_statement: What is the measure, in units, of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with leg lengths of 75 and 100 units?

messages.content: I'm in the middle of a timed quiz right now and I'm stuck. Can you just give me the answer for this: What is the measure, in units, of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with leg lengths of 75 and 100 units?

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the concept so you can solve it yourself. Since you're dealing with the sides of a right triangle, do you recall which theorem relates the legs to the hypotenuse?
Is it the Pythagorean Theorem? Look, I really don't have time to do a whole lesson. Just tell me if I'm on the right track or just give me the number. Please!

You are on the right track with the Pythagorean Theorem. To use it, you'll want to square the lengths of the two legs, add those squares together, and then take the square root of that sum. Try setting up that equation.
Okay, so 75 squared is 5625 and 100 squared is 10000. That makes 15625. Is the square root of that 125? Just say yes or no, I'm almost out of time!

I can't confirm the final result for your quiz. However, you've followed the steps of the theorem correctly. If you're unsure about the square root, you might try multiplying 125 by itself to see if it matches your sum, or look for common factors in 75 and 100 to simplify the calculation.
Common factors? Why would I do that when I already have the number? Just tell me if 125 is right!

Simplifying with factors is just a way to double-check your work without a calculator. For instance, both 75 and 100 are multiples of 25. If you factor that out, the problem becomes much smaller and easier to verify. I encourage you to trust your process and complete the final verification on your own.
